summary: Backend-only follow-up to iter301 (MOD fault emails). Iter301 suite re-run: 17/17 pass. New suite test_mod_fault_email_followup_iter302.py: 15/16 pass. All 6 requested items work: (1) dead steps_row code gone; (2) when the equipment has no serial but doc.serial_number does, the header shows 'Rower · S/N <doc serial>' in both emails and the Pulse and supplier subjects end with ' — S/N <doc serial>'. The submit flow was checked in-process by patching routes.bfpo._bridge_mod_fault_to_bfpo to set doc.serial_number. The equipment serial wins when both exist. No S/N text or 'None' appears when neither is set. (3) The Photos row is exactly 'N attached' (empty URLs not counted), with no 'shown below'. (4) HTML in steps_taken is escaped in the 'Steps taken on site' row of both emails, including the submit flow. (5) _confirmation_email_html escapes reporter name, machine, site, email, phone, ticket ref and priority. A missing phone renders blank, not 'None'. (6) _tracked_send: create_supplier_case was patched to sleep 3s, so notified_recipients was written at least 3s after the Pulse send. Pulse and supplier entries both still got delivered=True and message_id='TEST_mid'. The one failure is a new edge case: a serial of only spaces gives a blank 'S/N' in the Pulse subject and email headers. No real email was sent (resend guard never hit). All TEST_ data was deleted by id (0 left).

minor.endpoint: routes/mod_portal.py mod_fault_submit Pulse subject (line ~1834) + header lines in _escalation_email_html / _supplier_fault_email_html (lines 3630, 3731)
minor.issue: These don't .strip() the serial, unlike the supplier subject (line 1929) and the details table. An equipment serial of only spaces gives '[MOD Fault] ... — TEST_Rower — S/N    ' and 'R · S/N   ' in the header, while the supplier subject has no S/N and the table says 'Not on file'. Fix: compute serial = (eq.get('serial_number') or doc.get('serial_number') or '').strip() once and use it in all three places. No current DB equipment has a serial of only spaces, so impact is low.
Info: doc.serial_number is always copied from equipment.serial_number (line 1749), so in the live submit flow the doc fallback can't trigger. It only matters for other callers or re-sends. Not a bug.
